features: Bounded packed weapon visual cache and active-loadout preparation during map loading
Two pose samples per global frame for queued clip preparation, live rig restoration and weak-reference cancellation
Remote IK pose interpolation and display-cadence prepared animation playback
unchanged: XR LOD policy and distance thresholds
Local tracked pose latency and authoritative movement/hitboxes

weapon_after.scope: Weapon factory CPU time with native renderer, first factory use then two warm passes; each model lives six process frames so deferred warmup completes. Does not measure first-visible-frame GPU pipeline compilation, avatar attachment, gameplay or XR.

avatars_after.scope: 16 avatars, three shared VRMs, eight full-body/face and eight head/hands, half speaking; springs disabled. Reversed scenario order. XR policy is a synthetic XRCamera3D without headset/runtime, NOT VR rendering or headset timing. No map, networking, audio or gameplay. Script scopes are nested; render CPU is rendering only. Uncontrolled OS/GPU clocks.

limitations: Synthetic benchmarks on i7-12700 / Arc A770, without headset or controlled clocks.
Remote interpolation adds bounded presentation delay up to a solve interval and some render-frame work.
Synthetic XR-policy avatar scene has higher p95 frame times after interpolation; no overall FPS improvement is claimed.
First weapon preparation cost is moved to loading rather than eliminated.
Successful fixtures report an existing ObjectDB shutdown warning.
fixture_maintenance: Audio test reads the current generated weapon trim instead of a stale hardcoded attenuation.
TF visual test checks the enforced effective loadout.
Death fixture supplies the existing defusal visibility API.
Animation fixture explicitly enables springs, which now default off.
Rendered-motion fixture supplies the current lobby/defusal visibility APIs.
